generator.prompt: The first reference image is a TIGHTLY cropped character with almost no empty margin around her (a post-processed crop, not the original generation framing). Mentally place that same reference image inside a much larger, mostly empty 1024x1024 transparent canvas: she would occupy only the region from about x=230,y=344 to about x=555,y=904 (about 560 px tall, left-of-center, with generous empty margin above, below, to the left and especially to the right of her). Her neck/collar, where the hood meets her shoulders, sits at approximately x=344-506, y=434-467 in that same 1024x1024 canvas. The second reference image shows the scarf from the previous frame of this same breathing-idle loop, already correctly scaled and positioned in its own 1024x1024 canvas at this same character scale and neck location. Using that exact character scale and canvas framing, paint ONLY a long, wide, flowing fabric scarf in the same plain, flat, neutral medium-gray color as the second reference image (no other hue, no pattern, no shading gradient into a color, just neutral gray), tied around her neck at that same x/y location. Match the second reference image's scarf shape, drape and position almost exactly -- change it only by an almost imperceptible micro-sway of at most a few pixels at the very tip of the hem, nowhere near a breeze, gust, or dramatic drift; the overall silhouette must look essentially the same as the second reference image's scarf shape. Most of its length falls in the region below and slightly right of the neck point, mostly overlapping where her robe and torso would be (that overlap is correct and expected, since her body will be drawn on top of it afterward) -- do not draw the scarf away from that neck point out in the empty right two-thirds of the canvas. Wide and voluminous, clearly broader than a thin ribbon. Paint NOTHING else in the image: no character, no body, no face, no hands, no hood, no clothing, no background, no ground, no shadow, no text -- only the gray scarf shape, on the same size canvas with the same framing, fully transparent everywhere else, with no vignette or darkened backdrop of any kind. IMPORTANT: paint exactly ONE single opaque, solid gray scarf shape -- do not paint multiple overlapping, ghosted or semi-transparent copies of the scarf at different offsets; the scarf must be one continuous, fully opaque cloth shape, not several stacked layers.
